requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
State updates go through scripts/project_queue.py status and note ONLY. GOV.ORCH.5 forbids hand-editing project/*.json, and this movement is not an exception.

EVIDENCE BEFORE STATUS. For each item, first gather the proof and write it down, then set the status. An item you cannot prove closed stays open -- that is a correct result, not a failure of the movement.

Evidence means a file path plus what is in it, or a command plus its output. 'It looks done' is not evidence. A contract's own status line, a class that exists with the behaviour named, a migration file, a passing test -- those are evidence.
If an item is only PARTLY satisfied, do NOT set it done. Leave the status and add a note through the tool saying exactly which part is satisfied and which is not.
Commit early and often on the lane.
Do not merge to main. The Product Owner assistant reviews the diff and merges.
Do not run the full pytest suite. It creates untracked data/ and logs/ directories that the repository privacy gate then flags, failing a movement whose diff is clean.
Touch ONLY the backlog item ids this packet names. Another movement is running in parallel on a different, disjoint set of ids in the same file; editing an id outside your set will collide with it.
risks: Closing all seven because six status lines look alike, without reading what each workflow section actually required.
Treating 'a FROZEN contract exists' as proof the item is done when the item required more than the document.
Hand-editing the JSON because the tool is slower.
Touching an id belonging to the parallel movement and colliding with it.
Rounding a partly complete item up to done.

in: For EACH of the seven ids -- ui2_b0_c1_platform_schema_contract, ui2_b0_c2_job_execution_contract, ui2_b0_c3_identity_sessions_rbac_contract, ui2_b0_c4_capability_registry_gate_resolution_contract, ui2_b0_c5_amendments_bundle, ui2_b0_c6_capability_extraction_contract, ui2_b0_c7_backup_artefact_restore_engine_contract -- do this separately and record it separately.

Read the item's own target field to learn what it required. Several name 'workflow section 5 B0-N'; docs/design/UI2_0_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md is that workflow. Read the section the item names and take ITS definition of what B0-N required, rather than assuming the item was satisfied by the existence of a document.
Find the contract the item was to produce, read its status block, and record the exact status text and date.

Decide, per item: complete, partly complete, or not complete. Set status done for a complete one via 'python3 scripts/project_queue.py status --id <id> --set done'. Leave a partly complete or incomplete one alone and record why.

Record the evidence for every item through 'python3 scripts/project_queue.py note --id <id> --text ...' -- the contract path, its status text and date, and the workflow section that defined the requirement. Write the note for items you close AND for items you leave open.
If an item's contract is FROZEN but the workflow section required something beyond the contract -- an implementation, a test, a fixture -- say so and do NOT close the item.
out: Every backlog id outside the seven named above. A parallel movement is editing a disjoint set in this same file.
Changing any priority, target or title.
Deleting any item or any note.
Editing project/backlog.json, project/QUEUE.md or any project/*.json directly. The tool is the only write path.
Editing any design document, contract or FROZEN document.
Any source code change, any test change, anything under ui2/, utils/, scripts/ or application/.
Freezing, unfreezing or reviewing any contract. Reading a status line is not reviewing it.
Deciding that a contract frozen by an agent rather than by Product Owner review is or is not sufficient. Record what the status line says and move on.
